answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the cipher check immediately, the willow audit keeps the resolved set and the falcon replay publishes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 26 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 26 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 37 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
